frames.narration: A producer creates 20 items per second. The consumer can process only 8 per second. The buffer between them holds at most 5 items.
Items arrive faster than they leave, so the buffer fills up.
The buffer is full. With no limit, it would keep growing, using more memory and adding more delay until the process crashed.
A full buffer is a signal. It tells the producer: stop sending until there is room.
The consumer finishes an item and frees a slot. The buffer lets the producer send one more.
The producer now runs at 8 per second, the speed of the slowest stage. Memory stays flat and delay stays small. The alternative to waiting is to drop items, if losing some is acceptable.
